verses.1: When King Hezekiah heard this, he tore his clothes and covered himself with sackcloth and went into the house of the LORD.
verses.2: He sent Eliakim, who was in charge of the palace, Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, each wrapped in sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.
verses.3: They said to him, "This is what Hezekiah says: It is a day of trouble, rebuke, and disgrace. The child has come to the point of childbirth, but there is no strength to give birth.
verses.4: Perhaps the LORD your God will hear the words of Rabshakeh, the one sent by the king of Assyria, who his master has sent to mock a living God, and the LORD your God will vindicate the words you have heard. Pray for the survivors who remain."
verses.5: Then the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah.
verses.6: Isaiah said to them, "Tell your master, 'This is what the LORD says: Do not be afraid of the words you have heard, which the young men of the king of Assyria have used to mock me.
verses.7: I am going to put a spirit in him so that he will hear a report and return to his own land. I will cause him to fall by the sword in his land.'"
verses.8: Rabshakeh returned and found the king of Assyria fighting against Libnah, for he had heard that the king had left Lachish.
verses.9: A report reached him from Tirhakah, king of Cush: "You have gone out to fight against us, but I have heard of it and have sent messengers to Hezekiah, the king of Judah, saying:
verses.10: This is what Hezekiah, the king of Judah, says to you: Do not let your god, in whom you trust, deceive you by saying, 'Jerusalem will not be handed over to the king of Assyria.'
verses.11: You have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the lands, and yet you imagine that you will escape.
verses.12: Have the gods of the nations whom my ancestors destroyed—Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the people of Eden in Telassar—saved them?
verses.13: Where is the king of Hamath, the king of Arpad, the king of Sepharvaim, the king of Hittite Samaria? Did any of them save their land from my hand?
verses.14: Then Hezekiah took the letters from the hands of the messengers, read them, went up to the house of the LORD, and spread them out before the LORD.
verses.15: He prayed to the LORD, saying:
verses.16: "O LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, enthroned among the cherubim, you alone are God for all the kingdoms of the earth. You made the heavens and the earth.
verses.17: Listen, O LORD, and hear; open your eyes, O LORD, and see. Listen to the words that Sennacherib has sent to mock a living God.
verses.18: It is indeed true that the kings of Assyria have laid waste to all the lands and their people.
verses.19: They have burned their gods in the fire, for they are no gods but the work of human hands—wood and stone. So they were destroyed.
verses.20: Now, O LORD our God, deliver us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you alone are the LORD."
verses.21: Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent word to Hezekiah: "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says, whom you have prayed to about Sennacherib, the king of Assyria:
verses.22: 'This is the report from the LORD about him: She will mock you, Daughter of Zion; she will taunt you, Daughter of Jerusalem.
verses.23: 'Whom have you defied and insulted? Against whom have you raised your voice and lifted your eyes in pride? It is against the Holy One of Israel.
verses.24: 'Through your messengers you have defied the LORD. You said, "With my many chariots I have climbed to the heights of the mountains. I have cut down the tallest cedars of Lebanon and the choicest of its cypresses. I have come to the highest peaks of its forest.
verses.25: "I have dug wells and drunk water, and with the soles of my feet I have dried up every stream of the captured city."
verses.26: "Have you not heard? Long ago I made it, from ancient times I formed it. Now I have brought it to pass, that you would make desolate fortified cities into a heap of ruins.
verses.27: "Their inhabitants, with their hands, have made them desolate and ashamed. They have become like dry grass on rooftops, like withering grass in the fields, like new grain that has not matured.
verses.28: "I know your coming and going, your rising and setting. I know your anger toward me.
verses.29: "Your rage and your fury have come to me and have been heard, and I will put a bridle in your nose and a bit in your mouth. I will send you back along the path you came.
verses.30: "This is the sign for you: This year you will eat what grows by itself, and the next year what springs from that. In the third year you will sow and reap, you will plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
verses.31: "The survivors from the house of Judah will take root below and bear fruit above.
verses.32: "For from Jerusalem will come a remnant, and survivors from Mount Zion. The jealousy of the LORD of Hosts will do this."
verses.33: Therefore the LORD says regarding the king of Assyria, "He will not enter this city, nor will he shoot an arrow there, nor will he set up a siege ramp around it, nor will he throw a single wall around it.
verses.34: "By the road he came, he will return. To this city he will not come," says the LORD.
verses.35: "I will defend this city to save it for my own sake and for the sake of my servant David."
verses.36: So an angel of the LORD went out and struck down one hundred and eighty-five thousand men in the Assyrian camp. When they awoke in the morning, there were all the dead bodies—only corpses.
verses.37: Sennacherib, the king of Assyria, left, went back, and settled in Nineveh.
verses.38: While he was worshiping in the house of Nisroch, his god, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer struck him down with the sword. They fled into the land of Ararat, and Esarhaddon his son became king in his place.

notes:
Notes
- v. 11: "my ancestors destroyed" — the plural "ancestors" is used for clarity; the Hebrew is singular "father," but the context refers to Israel's history.
- v. 12: "Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the people of Eden in Telassar" — names of ancient locations destroyed by Assyria.
- v. 16: "O LORD of Hosts" — "of Hosts" is part of the divine title YHWH Tseva'ot, rendered "LORD of Hosts."
- v. 23: "the Holy One of Israel" — YHWH Qadosh Yisra'el, a common divine title in Isaiah.
- v. 35: "for the sake of my servant David" — "servant" is used for "doulos," but in this context, "servant" as a title for David is appropriate.
raw:
[1] When King Hezekiah heard this, he tore his clothes and covered himself with sackcloth and went into the house of the LORD.

[2] He sent Eliakim, who was in charge of the palace, Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, each wrapped in sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.

[3] They said to him, "This is what Hezekiah says: It is a day of trouble, rebuke, and disgrace. The child has come to the point of childbirth, but there is no strength to give birth.

[4] Perhaps the LORD your God will hear the words of Rabshakeh, the one sent by the king of Assyria, who his master has sent to mock a living God, and the LORD your God will vindicate the words you have heard. Pray for the survivors who remain."

[5] Then the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah.

[6] Isaiah said to them, "Tell your master, 'This is what the LORD says: Do not be afraid of the words you have heard, which the young men of the king of Assyria have used to mock me.

[7] I am going to put a spirit in him so that he will hear a report and return to his own land. I will cause him to fall by the sword in his land.'"

[8] Rabshakeh returned and found the king of Assyria fighting against Libnah, for he had heard that the king had left Lachish.

[9] A report reached him from Tirhakah, king of Cush: "You have gone out to fight against us, but I have heard of it and have sent messengers to Hezekiah, the king of Judah, saying:

[10] This is what Hezekiah, the king of Judah, says to you: Do not let your god, in whom you trust, deceive you by saying, 'Jerusalem will not be handed over to the king of Assyria.'

[11] You have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the lands, and yet you imagine that you will escape.

[12] Have the gods of the nations whom my ancestors destroyed—Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the people of Eden in Telassar—saved them?

[13] Where is the king of Hamath, the king of Arpad, the king of Sepharvaim, the king of Hittite Samaria? Did any of them save their land from my hand?

[14] Then Hezekiah took the letters from the hands of the messengers, read them, went up to the house of the LORD, and spread them out before the LORD.

[15] He prayed to the LORD, saying:

[16] "O LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, enthroned among the cherubim, you alone are God for all the kingdoms of the earth. You made the heavens and the earth.

[17] Listen, O LORD, and hear; open your eyes, O LORD, and see. Listen to the words that Sennacherib has sent to mock a living God.

[18] It is indeed true that the kings of Assyria have laid waste to all the lands and their people.

[19] They have burned their gods in the fire, for they are no gods but the work of human hands—wood and stone. So they were destroyed.

[20] Now, O LORD our God, deliver us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you alone are the LORD."

[21] Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent word to Hezekiah: "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says, whom you have prayed to about Sennacherib, the king of Assyria:

[22] 'This is the report from the LORD about him: She will mock you, Daughter of Zion; she will taunt you, Daughter of Jerusalem.

[23] 'Whom have you defied and insulted? Against whom have you raised your voice and lifted your eyes in pride? It is against the Holy One of Israel.

[24] 'Through your messengers you have defied the LORD. You said, "With my many chariots I have climbed to the heights of the mountains. I have cut down the tallest cedars of Lebanon and the choicest of its cypresses. I have come to the highest peaks of its forest.

[25] "I have dug wells and drunk water, and with the soles of my feet I have dried up every stream of the captured city."

[26] "Have you not heard? Long ago I made it, from ancient times I formed it. Now I have brought it to pass, that you would make desolate fortified cities into a heap of ruins.

[27] "Their inhabitants, with their hands, have made them desolate and ashamed. They have become like dry grass on rooftops, like withering grass in the fields, like new grain that has not matured.

[28] "I know your coming and going, your rising and setting. I know your anger toward me.

[29] "Your rage and your fury have come to me and have been heard, and I will put a bridle in your nose and a bit in your mouth. I will send you back along the path you came.

[30] "This is the sign for you: This year you will eat what grows by itself, and the next year what springs from that. In the third year you will sow and reap, you will plant vineyards and eat their fruit.

[31] "The survivors from the house of Judah will take root below and bear fruit above.

[32] "For from Jerusalem will come a remnant, and survivors from Mount Zion. The jealousy of the LORD of Hosts will do this."

[33] Therefore the LORD says regarding the king of Assyria, "He will not enter this city, nor will he shoot an arrow there, nor will he set up a siege ramp around it, nor will he throw a single wall around it.

[34] "By the road he came, he will return. To this city he will not come," says the LORD.

[35] "I will defend this city to save it for my own sake and for the sake of my servant David."

[36] So an angel of the LORD went out and struck down one hundred and eighty-five thousand men in the Assyrian camp. When they awoke in the morning, there were all the dead bodies—only corpses.

[37] Sennacherib, the king of Assyria, left, went back, and settled in Nineveh.

[38] While he was worshiping in the house of Nisroch, his god, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer struck him down with the sword. They fled into the land of Ararat, and Esarhaddon his son became king in his place.
